name: Discord Cache & Code Cache
whatIsIt: Discord stores a local copy of every video, audio message, GIF, image, and emoji loaded across your servers and direct messages.
whatHappens: Deleting this clears disk space immediately. It does NOT delete your chat history, server memberships, or account credentials. Discord simply re-downloads media as you view it.
manualSteps: Completely exit Discord (right-click the Discord icon in your system tray and select 'Quit Discord').
Press the Windows Key + R to open the Run dialog.
Type %appdata%\discord and hit Enter.
Delete the folders named 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'GPUCache'.

name: Spotify Offline Storage & Streaming Cache
whatIsIt: Spotify caches streamed song tracks locally on your C: drive to speed up playback and reduce bandwidth usage.
whatHappens: Wiping this cache reclaims several gigabytes. Your playlists and saved songs remain safe in your Spotify account, though downloaded songs for offline mode will need re-syncing.
manualSteps: Close Spotify.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Spotify, and press Enter.
Open the 'Storage' directory, select all files (Ctrl+A), and press Delete.

name: Steam Shader Pre-Caching & Download Bloat
whatIsIt: Steam saves graphics files for every game you play so levels load faster, and those large files stay behind even after you stop playing or uninstall a game.
whatHappens: Completely safe to clean. Your game saves and installed games are never touched.
manualSteps: Open Steam Settings > Downloads.
Scroll to Shader Pre-Caching and review space used.
Navigate to C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\shadercache and delete old game app-id folders.

name: Google Chrome Service Worker & CacheStorage
whatIsIt: Websites you visit in Chrome (like YouTube, Gmail, and online tools) quietly store gigabytes of offline files on your hard drive.
whatHappens: Frees up hidden browser storage right away. You stay signed in to your accounts and nothing important is lost.
manualSteps: Close Google Chrome.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default and hit Enter.
Locate 'Service Worker' and delete the 'CacheStorage' directory.

name: Windows WinSxS (Side-by-Side Component Store)
warning: DO NOT manually delete files directly inside WinSxS in File Explorer. Doing so will corrupt Windows updates and prevent your system from booting.
whatIsIt: Windows keeps old copies of update files in this folder in case it ever needs to undo a system update.
whatHappens: When cleaned safely using Windows built-in tools or SWEEPR Cleaner, old update leftovers are removed without harming your computer.
manualSteps: Right-click Start and choose 'Terminal (Admin)' or 'Command Prompt (Admin)'.
Type: dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore to check reclaimable space.
Type: dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup to safely purge superseded components.

name: Windows System Temp Folder
whatIsIt: Old setup files and temporary logs created by Windows updates and installers that are no longer needed.
whatHappens: Completely safe to delete. Any file currently being used by Windows is automatically skipped.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\Windows\Temp and press Enter (click Continue if prompted for administrator access).
Select all items with Ctrl+A and press Shift+Delete.
Check 'Do this for all current items' and click Skip if a file is currently in use.

name: User AppData Local Temp Directory
whatIsIt: Apps use this folder as a scratchpad for temporary files when opening downloads or installing updates, and often forget to clean it up.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Frees up gigabytes of wasted space immediately while skipping any files currently open.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %temp% and press Enter.
Select all files (Ctrl+A) and press Delete.
If Windows prompts that a file is open in another program, check 'Do this for all current items' and choose Skip.

name: Windows.old (Previous Windows Installation)
whatIsIt: When Windows upgrades to a major new version or build, it saves a complete backup of your previous OS files in C:\Windows.old so you can roll back.
whatHappens: If your PC has been running smoothly for more than 10 days after an update, deleting Windows.old is completely safe and reclaims 20+ GB.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage.
Click on 'Temporary files'.
Check 'Previous Windows installation(s)' and click 'Remove files'.

name: NVIDIA DirectX Shader Cache (DXCache)
whatIsIt: NVIDIA's graphics driver stores compiled DirectX 11 and DirectX 12 shader binaries in DXCache so games load faster without stuttering.
whatHappens: Deleting older shader cache files reclaims gigabytes of SSD space and fixes corrupted shader stutter after driver updates. Currently active files locked by the driver are safely skipped.
manualSteps: Close all running games and 3D applications.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\NVIDIA\DXCache and press Enter.
Select all files (Ctrl+A), press Delete, and click Skip for any files currently locked by the NVIDIA display driver.

name: NVIDIA OpenGL & Vulkan Shader Cache (GLCache)
whatIsIt: Contains pre-compiled OpenGL and Vulkan shader binaries generated by emulators, creative apps, and Vulkan games.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Games and OpenGL applications will cleanly rebuild fresh shaders on their next launch.
manualSteps: Exit any running games or creative software.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\NVIDIA\GLCache and hit Enter.
Delete the hexadecimal cache folders inside.

name: NVIDIA ProgramData NV_Cache & Installer Leftovers
whatIsIt: Legacy NVIDIA shader cache and driver telemetry staging files stored in ProgramData across GeForce driver updates.
whatHappens: Frees up gigabytes on your C: drive without affecting your current NVIDIA GeForce driver or Control Panel settings.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\NV_Cache and press Enter.
Select all files (Ctrl+A) and press Delete.
Skip any file currently in use by nvcontainer.exe.

name: AMD Radeon Adrenalin DXCache & VkCache
whatIsIt: AMD Radeon graphics drivers store compiled DirectX and Vulkan shaders in %LocalAppData%\AMD to speed up level loading.
whatHappens: Safely removes stale shaders from uninstalled games and resolves Radeon frame-pacing micro-stutter after driver updates.
manualSteps: Close all games or use AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition > Gaming > Graphics > Reset Shader Cache.
Alternatively, press Windows Key + R and type %localappdata%\AMD.
Open DxCache, DxcCache, and VkCache and delete old shader files.

name: Intel Arc & Iris Xe Graphics Shader Cache
whatIsIt: Intel Arc and integrated Iris Xe graphics drivers cache compiled DirectX shaders in %LocalAppData%\Intel\ShaderCache.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Reclaims SSD space and forces clean shader compilation for updated games.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Intel\ShaderCache and press Enter.
Select all cached shader files with Ctrl+A and press Delete.
Skip any files locked by the desktop window manager.

name: Epic Games Launcher Webcache & Crash Logs
whatIsIt: Epic Games Launcher embeds a Chromium browser that caches store videos, banners, and crash logs inside Saved\webcache.
whatHappens: Reclaims disk space and fixes blank black screen issues in the Epic Games Launcher store tab without affecting installed games.
manualSteps: Right-click the Epic Games Launcher system tray icon and click Exit.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\EpicGamesLauncher\Saved and press Enter.
Delete any folders starting with 'webcache' as well as the 'Logs' and 'Crashes' folders.

name: Steam Depotcache & Downloading Staging Bloat
whatIsIt: Steam stores compressed patch manifests and incomplete delta update chunks in depotcache and steamapps\downloading.
whatHappens: When no game updates are actively paused or downloading, clearing orphaned depotcache chunks reclaims up to 20 GB safely.
manualSteps: Ensure no games are currently downloading or paused in your Steam Library.
Open Steam > Settings > Downloads and click 'Clear Download Cache'.
Verify C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\depotcache is cleared of stale manifest files.

name: Blizzard Battle.net Agent & Blizzard Entertainment Cache
whatIsIt: Battle.net stores game patch indexes, promotional videos, and Chromium launcher caches inside ProgramData.
whatHappens: Safe to delete while Battle.net is closed. Fixes stuck game update loops in Call of Duty, Overwatch 2, Diablo IV, and World of Warcraft.
manualSteps: Exit the Battle.net desktop app completely.
Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\Blizzard Entertainment\Battle.net\Cache and press Enter.
Select all cache subfolders and delete them.

name: EA App & Origin Legacy Installer Cache
whatIsIt: The EA Desktop App caches store web assets, patch telemetry, and temporary installer packages in LocalAppData and ProgramData.
whatHappens: Clears gigabytes of launcher bloat and resolves missing library tile bugs without uninstalling your EA games.
manualSteps: Open the EA App menu (top-left) > Help > App Recovery > Clear Cache.
Or close EA App, press Windows Key + R, and navigate to %localappdata%\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop\cache.
Delete all cached files inside.

name: Ubisoft Connect Launcher Cache & Logs
whatIsIt: Ubisoft Connect stores temporary patch spool data, overlay screenshots, and HTTP caches in LocalAppData.
whatHappens: Frees up disk space and fixes Ubisoft Connect overlay lag without affecting game save files.
manualSteps: Quit Ubisoft Connect from the Windows system tray.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Ubisoft Game Launcher and press Enter.
Delete the contents of the 'cache' and 'logs' folders.

name: Riot Client, Valorant & League of Legends Logs & WebCache
whatIsIt: Valorant, League of Legends, and the Riot Client write verbose match logs, crash dumps, and CEF webcaches after every session.
whatHappens: 100% safe to clean when Riot games are closed. Frees up gigabytes of SSD space while preserving all keybinds and settings.
manualSteps: Exit Riot Client and any running Riot games.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\VALORANT\Saved and press Enter.
Delete the contents of the 'Logs', 'Crashes', and 'webcache' folders.

name: Roblox Temporary Texture & HTTP Asset Cache
whatIsIt: Every Roblox experience downloads custom 3D meshes, audio assets, and textures into %Temp%\Roblox\http and sounds.
whatHappens: Deleting %Temp%\Roblox immediately reclaims up to 12 GB of space without affecting your Roblox account or saved progress.
manualSteps: Close the Roblox Player and Roblox Studio.
Press Windows Key + R, type %temp%\Roblox and press Enter.
Select all folders (http, sounds, textures) with Ctrl+A and press Delete.

name: Minecraft Launcher Webcache, Logs & Crash Reports
whatIsIt: Heavily modded Minecraft installations and the official launcher accumulate gigabytes of compressed debug logs, crash reports, and Chromium webcache files.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your Minecraft worlds (saves), resourcepacks, and mods folders are never touched.
manualSteps: Close the Minecraft Launcher.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\.minecraft and press Enter.
Delete the contents of 'logs', 'crash-reports', and 'webcache2' (do NOT delete 'saves').

name: GOG Galaxy Webcache & Installer Temp
whatIsIt: GOG Galaxy caches high-resolution game backgrounds, store assets, and offline installer manifests in ProgramData\GOG.com\Galaxy\webcache.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. GOG Galaxy re-fetches artwork for active games on demand without touching installed games.
manualSteps: Exit GOG Galaxy from the system tray.
Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\GOG.com\Galaxy\webcache and press Enter.
Delete the cached asset folders inside.

name: HoYoPlay & Genshin Impact Temp Update Packages
whatIsIt: HoYoPlay and Genshin Impact store temporary zip chunks and voiceover staging archives during major version updates.
whatHappens: Removing leftover update staging files reclaims up to 22 GB after a patch completes.
manualSteps: Ensure HoYoPlay is not currently downloading an update.
Open HoYoPlay Settings > Clear Downloaded Resource Cache.
Remove any leftover .tmp or .zip_temp archives in the game installation folder.

name: VRChat World & Avatar Cache (Cache-WindowsPlayer)
whatIsIt: VRChat downloads every custom user avatar and 3D world you visit into AppData\LocalLow\VRChat, easily growing past 20–30 GB.
whatHappens: 100% safe to clear. Frees up massive SSD space while keeping your account, friends list, and uploaded avatars intact.
manualSteps: Exit VRChat.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\..\LocalLow\VRChat\VRChat\Cache-WindowsPlayer and press Enter.
Select all cache folders and delete them.

name: FiveM Server Asset & Priv Cache
whatIsIt: FiveM downloads custom vehicles, textures, and map scripts for every GTA V roleplay server you join into data\server-cache-priv.
whatHappens: Clears tens of gigabytes of outdated RP server mods and fixes FiveM texture streaming crashes.
manualSteps: Close FiveM.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\FiveM\FiveM.app\data and press Enter.
Delete 'cache', 'server-cache', and 'server-cache-priv' (leave the 'game-storage' folder intact).

name: osu! Staging & Beatmap Extraction Temp
whatIsIt: osu! stores replay caches, crash logs, and temporary beatmap extraction buffers inside %LocalAppData%\osu!.
whatHappens: Cleans temporary replay and log bloat without touching your Songs or Skins folders.
manualSteps: Close osu!.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\osu! and press Enter.
Delete the contents of the 'Logs' folder (never delete 'Songs' or 'Skins').

name: Razer Synapse 3 Installer Cache & Logs
whatIsIt: Razer Synapse and Razer Cortex accumulate multi-gigabyte service logs and cached module installers in C:\ProgramData\Razer.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your mouse DPI profiles, macros, and Chroma lighting settings remain untouched.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\Razer\Synapse3\Log and press Enter.
Select all old log files (Ctrl+A) and delete them.
Skip the current active log file if Synapse is running.

name: Corsair iCUE Update Packages & Telemetry Logs
whatIsIt: Corsair iCUE stores verbose sensor polling logs, crash dumps, and downloaded plugin update packages.
whatHappens: Frees up disk space on C: without affecting your fan curves or RGB profiles.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Corsair and press Enter.
Open the 'logs' directory inside your iCUE folder and delete old log files.

name: Adobe Premiere Pro & After Effects Common Media Cache
whatIsIt: Premiere Pro and After Effects generate uncompressed conformed audio (.cfa) and peak (.pek) cache files for every video clip imported.
whatHappens: Deleting old Media Cache Files reclaims 10–60 GB of SSD space. Your Premiere project files (.prproj) and source footage are untouched.
manualSteps: Close Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Adobe\Common and press Enter.
Delete the contents of 'Media Cache Files', 'Media Cache', and 'Peak Files'.

name: Adobe After Effects Disk & Frame Preview Cache
whatIsIt: After Effects caches rendered RAM-preview frames directly to your SSD so timelines play back smoothly during editing.
whatHappens: 100% safe to purge between projects. Reclaims massive NVMe space without affecting saved compositions.
manualSteps: In After Effects, go to Edit > Purge > All Memory & Disk Cache.
Or close After Effects, navigate to %localappdata%\Temp\Adobe, and delete the After Effects Disk Cache folder.

name: Adobe Photoshop Orphaned Scratch Temp Files
whatIsIt: When Adobe Photoshop closes unexpectedly or handles large multi-layer PSDs, it leaves behind multi-gigabyte 'Photoshop Temp' scratch files in %Temp%.
whatHappens: While Photoshop is closed, deleting orphaned 'Photoshop Temp*' files is 100% safe and fixes 'Scratch Disks Are Full' errors.
manualSteps: Completely close Adobe Photoshop.
Press Windows Key + R, type %temp% and press Enter.
Delete any files starting with 'Photoshop Temp' or ' ~PST'.

name: Adobe Creative Cloud Installer & Patch Staging Cache
whatIsIt: Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop caches downloaded application setup payloads and patch archives in C:\ProgramData\Adobe\Installer.
whatHappens: Safe to remove once all Adobe updates have finished installing.
manualSteps: Ensure no Adobe apps are currently updating in Creative Cloud.
Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\Adobe\Installer and press Enter.
Delete leftover temporary installer archives.

name: DaVinci Resolve CacheClip & Optimized Media Bloat
whatIsIt: DaVinci Resolve renders uncompressed proxy frames and Fusion node caches into the CacheClip folder on your system drive.
whatHappens: Safe to delete for completed projects. Resolve simply re-renders any active timeline cache if you reopen an old project.
manualSteps: Close DaVinci Resolve (or use Playback > Delete Render Cache > All inside Resolve).
Open your Videos\CacheClip folder in File Explorer.
Delete old project cache UUID folders.

name: CapCut Desktop Proxy & Render Cache
whatIsIt: CapCut for Windows caches downloaded stock transitions, stickers, auto-captions, and proxy video renders in %LocalAppData%\CapCut.
whatHappens: Reclaims up to 25 GB of C: drive space while keeping your active video drafts intact.
manualSteps: Close CapCut Desktop.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\CapCut\User Data\Cache and press Enter.
Delete the contents of the 'effect', 'music', and 'renderCache' directories.

name: Blender Fluid, Smoke & Autosave Temp Cache
whatIsIt: Blender writes temporary physics bakes, EXR render buffers, and session quit.blend files into %Temp%\blender_*.
whatHappens: Safe to delete once you have saved your .blend project and closed Blender.
manualSteps: Save your work and close Blender.
Press Windows Key + R, type %temp% and press Enter.
Delete all folders beginning with 'blender_'.

name: Figma Desktop Font, Canvas & GPU Cache
whatIsIt: Figma's Electron desktop app caches high-DPI design canvases, vector assets, and WebGL textures locally on your drive.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete because all Figma files live in the cloud. Clears local disk bloat and fixes canvas WebGL memory errors.
manualSteps: Quit the Figma desktop app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Figma and press Enter.
Delete the 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'GPUCache' folders.

name: Canva Desktop Asset & Template Cache
whatIsIt: The Canva Windows app caches template previews, stock photos, and Service Worker assets inside %AppData%\Canva.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your cloud designs and account login are completely preserved.
manualSteps: Close the Canva desktop app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Canva and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'Service Worker\CacheStorage'.

name: OBS Studio Browser Source Cache & Session Logs
whatIsIt: OBS Studio caches Chromium browser source overlays (StreamElements, Twitch alerts) and session logs in %AppData%\obs-studio.
whatHappens: Frees up disk space and fixes frozen OBS Browser Source overlays without touching your scenes or encoder profiles.
manualSteps: Close OBS Studio.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\obs-studio and press Enter.
Delete old files inside 'logs', 'crashes', and 'plugin_config\obs-browser\Cache'.

name: Audacity Unsaved Audio Block Temp Data
whatIsIt: Audacity stores uncompressed 32-bit float audio undo blocks in %LocalAppData%\Audacity\SessionData while editing recordings.
whatHappens: Once your audio project is exported and Audacity is closed, orphaned SessionData files can be safely deleted.
manualSteps: Save your project and exit Audacity.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Audacity\SessionData and press Enter.
Delete any leftover orphaned temporary project files.

name: AutoCAD & Autodesk WebServices Cache & .ac$ Temp
whatIsIt: AutoCAD, Revit, and Fusion 360 leave behind temporary drawing lock files (.ac$, .sv$) and Autodesk Desktop App installer caches.
whatHappens: Safe to clean when all Autodesk applications are closed.
manualSteps: Save all drawings and exit AutoCAD/Autodesk apps.
Press Windows Key + R, type %temp% and press Enter.
Delete stale .ac$ and Autodesk installer staging folders.

name: Unity Editor Asset Store & GI Cache
whatIsIt: Unity caches every downloaded Asset Store package, UPM registry tarball, and Global Illumination (GI) bake in AppData.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Unity Package Manager can re-download any package you need from your Unity account.
manualSteps: Close Unity Hub and the Unity Editor.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Unity\cache and press Enter.
Delete the 'npm' and 'packages' cache folders.

name: Unreal Engine Common DerivedDataCache (DDC)
whatIsIt: Unreal Engine 5 stores compiled shaders, texture mipmaps, and mesh distance fields in DerivedDataCache across all projects.
whatHappens: 100% safe to clean. Reclaims up to 50 GB from old UE4/UE5 projects without altering your project source files.
manualSteps: Close Unreal Editor and Epic Games Launcher.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\UnrealEngine\Common\DerivedDataCache and press Enter.
Select all cached subfolders and delete them.

name: Adobe Lightroom Classic Camera Raw Cache
whatIsIt: Adobe Camera Raw and Lightroom Classic store fast-load RAW image previews inside %LocalAppData%\Adobe\CameraRaw\Cache2.
whatHappens: Completely safe to delete. Your original RAW photos and Lightroom catalog edits are untouched.
manualSteps: Close Lightroom Classic and Adobe Bridge.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Adobe\CameraRaw\Cache2 and press Enter.
Delete all cached preview files.

name: VLC Media Player Album Art & Shader Cache
whatIsIt: VLC Media Player caches album art thumbnails and Direct3D video output shaders inside %AppData%\vlc.
whatHappens: Clears cached media metadata and frees disk space safely.
manualSteps: Close VLC Media Player.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\vlc and press Enter.
Delete the 'art' folder and any .cache files.

name: Microsoft Teams (New & Classic) EBWebView Cache
whatIsIt: Microsoft Teams for Windows 11 uses Edge WebView2 to cache meeting backgrounds, shared files, and chat media locally.
whatHappens: Fixes Teams freezing/status bugs and reclaims up to 9 GB without deleting your chat history or calendar.
manualSteps: Right-click the Microsoft Teams icon in the taskbar and click Quit.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Packages\MSTeams_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalCache\Microsoft\MSTeams and press Enter.
Delete the 'EBWebView' cache directory.

name: Slack Desktop Cache & Service Worker Storage
whatIsIt: Slack's Electron desktop client caches every image, PDF preview, and emoji loaded across all connected workspaces.
whatHappens: Frees up several gigabytes of SSD space while keeping all your Slack workspaces logged in.
manualSteps: Completely quit Slack (Ctrl+Q).
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Slack and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', 'GPUCache', and 'Service Worker\CacheStorage'.

name: Zoom Workplace WebView Cache & Logs
whatIsIt: Zoom caches virtual backgrounds, avatar assets, whiteboard caches, and encrypted diagnostic logs in %AppData%\Zoom.
whatHappens: Safe to delete when not in an active meeting. Local MP4 meeting recordings in Documents\Zoom are never touched.
manualSteps: Exit the Zoom Workplace app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Zoom and press Enter.
Delete the contents of 'logs' and 'data\WebviewCache'.

name: Telegram Desktop Media & Video Cache (tdata\user_data)
whatIsIt: Telegram Desktop automatically downloads and caches photos, voice notes, and large channel videos inside tdata\user_data.
whatHappens: Deleting the cache and media_cache folders reclaims up to 25 GB while keeping your Telegram account logged in and all cloud messages safe.
manualSteps: Open Telegram Desktop > Settings > Advanced > Manage Local Storage > Clear All.
Or exit Telegram, press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Telegram Desktop\tdata\user_data and press Enter.
Delete the 'cache' and 'media_cache' folders (never delete key_datas).

name: WhatsApp for Windows UWP Media & WebCache
whatIsIt: The Windows 11 WhatsApp app stores temporary voice notes, video previews, and database WAL logs in its UWP LocalCache.
whatHappens: Clears gigabytes of duplicate media cache without unlinking your phone or deleting WhatsApp chat history.
manualSteps: Close WhatsApp on your PC.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Packages\5319275A.WhatsAppDesktop_cv1g1gvanyjgm\LocalState and press Enter.
Delete temporary cache files inside LocalCache and TempState.

name: Microsoft Edge Cache, Code Cache & Service Worker Bloat
whatIsIt: Even if you use another primary browser, Windows 11 background widgets and WebView components populate Microsoft Edge's Cache and Service Worker folders.
whatHappens: Reclaims gigabytes of hidden disk space without erasing saved passwords, favorites, or open tabs.
manualSteps: Close Microsoft Edge.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default and press Enter.
Delete the 'Cache', 'Code Cache', 'GPUCache', and 'Service Worker\CacheStorage' directories.

name: Brave Browser Cache & Service Worker Storage
whatIsIt: Brave stores cached web scripts, video chunks, and PWA Service Worker caches inside %LocalAppData%\BraveSoftware.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Brave Rewards, bookmarks, extensions, and saved logins are untouched.
manualSteps: Close Brave Browser.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\Default and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'Service Worker\CacheStorage'.

name: Mozilla Firefox cache2 & startupCache
whatIsIt: Firefox stores disk-cached images, compiled JS bytecode, and offline DOM storage in LocalAppData\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles.
whatHappens: Frees up disk space immediately while keeping bookmarks, cookies, and extensions in Roaming AppData safe.
manualSteps: Close Mozilla Firefox.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles and press Enter.
Open your profile folder and delete 'cache2' and 'startupCache'.

name: Opera & Opera GX Browser Cache & Media Cache
whatIsIt: Opera GX caches custom animated wallpapers, Twitch/Discord sidebar assets, and Chromium HTTP caches in LocalAppData.
whatHappens: Safely reclaims several gigabytes without resetting your Opera GX mods, bookmarks, or workspaces.
manualSteps: Close Opera GX.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Opera Software\Opera GX Stable and press Enter.
Delete the 'Cache' and 'System Cache' folders.

name: Vivaldi Browser Cache & Service Worker Bloat
whatIsIt: Vivaldi stores Chromium HTTP caches, GPU shader caches, and Service Worker blobs inside %LocalAppData%\Vivaldi.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. All tab stacks, mail databases, and saved passwords remain intact.
manualSteps: Close Vivaldi.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Vivaldi\User Data\Default and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'Service Worker\CacheStorage'.

name: Notion Desktop App Cache & Asset Cache
whatIsIt: Notion's desktop client caches offline database views, embedded PDFs, and electron app bundles in %AppData%\Notion.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your Notion workspaces sync from the cloud and stay signed in.
manualSteps: Quit the Notion desktop app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Notion and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and old folders inside 'assetCache'.

name: Obsidian Electron Cache & GPUCache
whatIsIt: Obsidian's Electron shell stores Chromium rendering caches in %AppData%\obsidian while your actual markdown notes live in your Vault folder.
whatHappens: Cleans Chromium rendering cache without touching your Markdown vaults or community plugins.
manualSteps: Close Obsidian.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\obsidian and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'GPUCache'.

name: Microsoft Outlook SecureTemp Attachments Cache (Content.Outlook)
whatIsIt: Every time you double-click an email attachment in classic Outlook, Windows saves a hidden read-only copy inside Content.Outlook.
whatHappens: Safely removes duplicate opened attachment copies while leaving the original emails and attachments in your inbox untouched.
manualSteps: Close Microsoft Outlook.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\Content.Outlook and press Enter.
Delete the temporary attachment files inside.

name: Microsoft OneDrive Setup & Telemetry Log Bloat
whatIsIt: OneDrive writes continuous sync telemetry (.odl, .odlgz) and keeps previous client installer binaries in %LocalAppData%\Microsoft\OneDrive.
whatHappens: Deletes gigs of sync logs without affecting any of your OneDrive cloud or local files.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\logs and press Enter.
Delete old .odl and .odlgz log files.
Skip the single log file currently open by OneDrive.exe.

name: Dropbox Hidden .dropbox.cache Staging Folder
whatIsIt: Dropbox maintains a hidden .dropbox.cache directory inside your Dropbox folder containing deleted file staging chunks and delta sync temp files.
whatHappens: Emptying .dropbox.cache immediately frees local SSD space without deleting active files in your Dropbox.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\Dropbox\.dropbox.cache and press Enter.
Select all temporary folders inside .dropbox.cache and press Delete.

name: Apple Devices & iTunes Old iOS Firmware (.ipsw) Cache
whatIsIt: When updating or restoring an iPhone or iPad via Windows, iTunes / Apple Devices downloads 7–9 GB .ipsw firmware files that stay on your C: drive forever.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete after your iPhone update is complete. Reclaims 6–25 GB instantly.
manualSteps: Close iTunes or the Apple Devices app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Apple Computer\iTunes\iPhone Software Updates and press Enter.
Delete old .ipsw firmware files.

name: Signal Desktop Electron Cache & Temp Logs
whatIsIt: Signal Desktop caches GPU textures, spellcheck dictionaries, and diagnostic logs in %AppData%\Signal.
whatHappens: Frees disk space safely while keeping your encrypted message database (sql) and linked device keys untouched.
manualSteps: Close Signal Desktop.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Signal and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', 'GPUCache', and 'logs' (do NOT delete 'sql' or 'config.json').

name: Mozilla Thunderbird Mail Cache (cache2)
whatIsIt: Thunderbird caches remote HTML email images, RSS feed enclosures, and indexed attachment previews in LocalAppData.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your IMAP/POP3 mail folders in Roaming AppData are never touched.
manualSteps: Close Mozilla Thunderbird.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Thunderbird\Profiles and press Enter.
Open your profile folder and delete the 'cache2' directory.

name: Visual Studio Code CachedData, CachedExtensionVSIXs & Logs
whatIsIt: VS Code retains V8 bytecode caches for every past VS Code version in CachedData and keeps downloaded .vsix installers in CachedExtensionVSIXs.
whatHappens: 100% safe to clean. All installed extensions, keybindings, and settings.json remain intact.
manualSteps: Close Visual Studio Code.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Code and press Enter.
Delete 'CachedData', 'CachedExtensionVSIXs', 'Cache', and 'logs'.

name: Node.js npm _cacache & npx Temp Cache
whatIsIt: npm stores a compressed tarball of every JavaScript package version ever installed across all projects in %LocalAppData%\npm-cache.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Existing node_modules folders in your projects continue working normally.
manualSteps: Open Terminal or PowerShell and run: npm cache clean --force.
Or navigate to %localappdata%\npm-cache and delete '_cacache' and '_npx'.

name: pnpm Content-Addressable Store & Metadata Cache
whatIsIt: pnpm caches registry metadata and unreferenced package blobs from deleted JavaScript repositories.
whatHappens: Running pnpm store prune or clearing pnpm-cache removes unreferenced packages without breaking active projects.
manualSteps: Open Terminal and run: pnpm store prune.
Delete %localappdata%\pnpm-cache to clear stale registry metadata.

name: Yarn Global Package Cache (%LocalAppData%\Yarn\Cache)
whatIsIt: Yarn caches zip archives of every downloaded npm dependency in %LocalAppData%\Yarn\Cache.
whatHappens: Completely safe to clean. Active projects retain their installed dependencies.
manualSteps: Run 'yarn cache clean' in your terminal.
Or press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Yarn\Cache and delete the cached folders.

name: Rust Cargo Registry Crate & Git Cache (.cargo\registry)
whatIsIt: Rust's Cargo package manager keeps every downloaded .crate archive and unpacked source tree in %UserProfile%\.cargo\registry.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Your installed cargo binaries (.cargo\bin) and rustup toolchains are untouched.
manualSteps: Ensure no cargo build is currently running.
Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\.cargo\registry and press Enter.
Delete the 'cache' and 'src' folders.

name: Python pip Wheel & HTTP Download Cache
whatIsIt: Python's pip installer caches large AI/ML wheels (PyTorch, CUDA, TensorFlow, NumPy) in %LocalAppData%\pip\Cache.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Virtual environments (venv/conda) and installed Python packages are not affected.
manualSteps: Run 'pip cache purge' in Command Prompt or PowerShell.
Or navigate to %localappdata%\pip\Cache and delete all files.

name: .NET NuGet HTTP & Temp Cache
whatIsIt: Visual Studio and the .NET SDK cache downloaded NuGet HTTP responses and scratch packages in %LocalAppData%\NuGet.
whatHappens: Safely reclaims gigabytes of SSD space; Visual Studio automatically restores any needed package on build.
manualSteps: Run 'dotnet nuget locals http-cache --clear' and 'dotnet nuget locals temp --clear' in Terminal.
Or delete %localappdata%\NuGet\v3-cache manually.

name: Gradle Build Cache & Wrapper Distributions (.gradle\caches)
whatIsIt: Android Studio and Java/Kotlin builds accumulate multiple gigabytes of old Gradle wrapper versions, build caches, and daemon logs in .gradle.
whatHappens: Safe to clean when Android Studio/IntelliJ is closed. Reclaims up to 35 GB of SSD space.
manualSteps: Close Android Studio and run 'gradle --stop' to stop background daemons.
Navigate to %userprofile%\.gradle.
Delete old daemon logs and unused transform caches inside .gradle\caches.

name: JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, RustRover) Caches
whatIsIt: JetBrains IDEs store huge local history indexes, AST caches, and old IDE version folders inside %LocalAppData%\JetBrains.
whatHappens: Deleting old IDE version caches reclaims 10+ GB without touching your settings or plugins in %AppData%\JetBrains.
manualSteps: Close all JetBrains IDEs.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\JetBrains and press Enter.
Delete folders belonging to older uninstalled IDE versions (e.g., IdeaIC2024.1) and clear the 'log' directories.

name: Android SDK System Image Download Intermediates
whatIsIt: The Android SDK Manager leaves multi-gigabyte zip archives in .temp and .downloadIntermediates after installing system images or NDKs.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete when SDK Manager is closed. Installed Android emulators and SDK platforms remain intact.
manualSteps: Close Android Studio.
Navigate to %localappdata%\Android\Sdk.
Delete the '.temp' and '.downloadIntermediates' folders.

name: Docker Desktop CrashDumps, Log Bloat & Dangling Build Cache
whatIsIt: Docker Desktop on Windows 11 accumulates dangling container layers, BuildKit caches, and verbose host logs in %LocalAppData%\Docker.
whatHappens: Pruning dangling build cache and clearing Docker logs reclaims tens of gigabytes without removing running containers.
manualSteps: Open Terminal and run: docker builder prune -f && docker image prune -f.
Navigate to %localappdata%\Docker\log and delete old log files.

name: PHP Composer Package Archive Cache
whatIsIt: PHP's Composer dependency manager caches downloaded zip packages and Packagist JSON metadata in %LocalAppData%\Composer.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Existing vendor folders in your PHP projects are untouched.
manualSteps: Run 'composer clear-cache' in your terminal.
Or delete %localappdata%\Composer\files and repo.

name: Go Compiler Build Cache (%LocalAppData%\go-build)
whatIsIt: The Go compiler caches incremental object files for every package ever compiled inside %LocalAppData%\go-build.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Go automatically rebuilds only active project object files on the next 'go build'.
manualSteps: Run 'go clean -cache' in PowerShell or Command Prompt.
Or delete all subfolders inside %localappdata%\go-build.

name: Apache Maven Corrupted .lastUpdated & Temp Artifacts
whatIsIt: Maven repositories accumulate failed download locks (.lastUpdated) and snapshot build leftovers in %UserProfile%\.m2\repository.
whatHappens: Removing .lastUpdated lock files and stale snapshots fixes broken Maven builds and reclaims gigabytes.
manualSteps: Close your Java IDE.
Open %userprofile%\.m2\repository and remove stale snapshot or .lastUpdated files.

name: Postman Desktop Logs & Chromium Cache
whatIsIt: Postman caches large API response bodies, Electron GPU shaders, and rotating logs in %AppData%\Postman.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your API collections, environments, and workspace sync remain intact.
manualSteps: Quit Postman.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Postman and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', 'GPUCache', and 'logs'.

name: Cursor & AI Code Editor CachedData & VSIX Bloat
whatIsIt: AI code editors built on VS Code (such as Cursor) keep old release CachedData bundles and downloaded extension VSIXs across frequent auto-updates.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete while the editor is closed. All settings, extensions, and project indexes remain intact.
manualSteps: Close Cursor.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Cursor and press Enter.
Delete 'CachedData', 'CachedExtensionVSIXs', and 'Cache'.

name: 7-Zip & WinRAR Orphaned Archive Extraction Temp (7zO* / Rar$*)
whatIsIt: When you open or drag a file directly out of a .zip, .7z, or .rar archive without extracting it first, 7-Zip and WinRAR unpack it into hidden %Temp%\7z* or Rar$* folders.
whatHappens: Deleting orphaned 7z* and Rar$* temp folders reclaims gigabytes of forgotten archive extractions.
manualSteps: Close 7-Zip and WinRAR.
Press Windows Key + R, type %temp% and press Enter.
Delete all folders starting with '7z' or 'Rar$'.

name: Plex Media Server Transcode & PhotoTranscoder Cache
whatIsIt: Plex Media Server caches resized poster thumbnails and temporary video transcode segments in %LocalAppData%\Plex Media Server\Cache.
whatHappens: Safe to clear when no stream is actively playing. Your media library metadata and watch history are preserved.
manualSteps: Ensure no Plex stream is actively transcoding.
Navigate to %localappdata%\Plex Media Server\Cache.
Delete the contents of 'PhotoTranscoder' and 'Transcode'.

name: Grammarly for Windows Logs & WebView Cache
whatIsIt: Grammarly's Windows overlay writes daily diagnostic logs and WebView caches in %LocalAppData%\Grammarly.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your Grammarly login and custom dictionary remain untouched.
manualSteps: Exit Grammarly from the system tray.
Navigate to %localappdata%\Grammarly and delete old log files.

name: Evernote Electron Cache & Temp Attachments
whatIsIt: Evernote 10+ uses an Electron shell that caches rendered note previews and web assets in %AppData%\Evernote\Cache.
whatHappens: Clears Chromium cache bloat while keeping your synced notebooks safe.
manualSteps: Quit Evernote.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Evernote and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'GPUCache'.

name: Logitech G HUB Update Cache & CrashDumps
whatIsIt: Logitech G HUB stores downloaded update depots and diagnostic logs inside C:\ProgramData\LGHUB.
whatHappens: Removing old depot archives frees disk space without deleting your mouse/keyboard profiles in %LocalAppData%\LGHUB\settings.db.
manualSteps: Verify G HUB is not actively updating.
Check C:\ProgramData\LGHUB and remove stale log or temp files (keep settings.db in LocalAppData).

name: Elgato Stream Deck & Wave Link Cache & Logs
whatIsIt: Elgato Stream Deck and Wave Link write rotating plugin logs and icon caches in %AppData%\Elgato.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Your Stream Deck button layouts and profiles are stored separately in ProfilesV2.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Elgato\StreamDeck\logs and press Enter.
Select all old .log files and delete them.

name: Adobe Acrobat Reader Setup Files & ARM Update Cache
whatIsIt: Adobe Acrobat and Reader store full MSI patch installers in C:\ProgramData\Adobe\ARM and font/search caches in LocalAppData.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete after updates finish installing.
manualSteps: Close Adobe Acrobat / Reader.
Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\Adobe\ARM and press Enter.
Delete old downloaded patch folders.

name: Google Drive for Desktop (DriveFS) Logs & Crashpad
whatIsIt: Google Drive for Desktop stores verbose sync trace logs and crash dumps in %LocalAppData%\Google\DriveFS.
whatHappens: Safe to delete the Logs and Crashpad folders. Never delete the numbered account content_cache folder while files are unsynced.
manualSteps: Pause or exit Google Drive for Desktop.
Navigate to %localappdata%\Google\DriveFS.
Delete the contents of 'Logs' and 'Crashpad\reports'.

name: Skype for Windows Media & WebView Cache
whatIsIt: Skype caches shared photos, video previews, and Chromium cache files locally in %AppData%.
whatHappens: Frees disk space without removing your cloud conversation history.
manualSteps: Quit Skype.
Navigate to %appdata%\Microsoft\Skype for Desktop and delete 'Cache' and 'GPUCache'.

name: TIDAL HiFi Lossless Audio Streaming Cache
whatIsIt: Because TIDAL streams uncompressed FLAC/HiRes audio, its local desktop cache in %AppData%\TIDAL grows rapidly to 10+ GB.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Playlists and favorite tracks remain synced to your TIDAL account.
manualSteps: Close the TIDAL desktop app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\TIDAL and press Enter.
Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'Service Worker\CacheStorage'.

name: qBittorrent GeoIP & Orphaned .torrent Cache
whatIsIt: qBittorrent caches execution logs and temporary RSS feeds inside %LocalAppData%\qBittorrent.
whatHappens: Clearing logs frees space without affecting active torrents in BT_backup.
manualSteps: Close qBittorrent.
Navigate to %localappdata%\qBittorrent\logs and delete old log files.

name: Anki Flashcard Backup & Media Trash Cache
whatIsIt: Anki retains dozens of historical collection.apkg backups and deleted flashcard media inside media.trash.
whatHappens: Emptying media.trash and old backups frees disk space while keeping your active flashcard decks safe.
manualSteps: In Anki, click Tools > Check Media > Empty Trash.
Or navigate to %appdata%\Anki2 and remove media.trash.

name: Windows Update Download Cache (SoftwareDistribution\Download)
whatIsIt: Windows Update downloads compressed cumulative updates and feature packs into C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download before installing them.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. It removes leftover installation packages and also fixes stuck Windows Update error codes.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files, or stop the 'wuauserv' service.
Navigate to C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download in File Explorer.
Select all files inside the Download folder (Ctrl+A) and press Delete.

name: Windows Delivery Optimization P2P Cache
whatIsIt: Windows 10 and 11 store peer-to-peer update and Microsoft Store app chunks in the DeliveryOptimization Cache folder to share with other PCs on your network.
whatHappens: Completely safe to delete. Reclaims gigabytes of SSD space immediately.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Delivery Optimization Files'.
Click 'Remove files' at the top.

name: Windows Prefetch Application Launch Cache
whatIsIt: Windows tracks how applications start up in .pf trace files inside C:\Windows\Prefetch, including hundreds of dead traces from uninstalled programs.
whatHappens: Safe to purge periodically when cluttered with old uninstalled app traces; Windows automatically rebuilds fresh traces for your current apps.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\Windows\Prefetch and press Enter (click Continue as Admin).
Select old .pf files (Ctrl+A) and press Delete.

name: Windows Installer Orphaned Patch Cache (C:\Windows\Installer)
warning: Never delete active .msi or .msp files directly from the root C:\Windows\Installer folder, or installed apps won't be able to uninstall. Only clean $PatchCache$ or verified orphaned patches.
whatIsIt: Windows caches baseline files inside C:\Windows\Installer\$PatchCache$\Managed to speed up MSI repairs.
whatHappens: Cleaning $PatchCache$\Managed or orphaned installer packages reclaims up to 25 GB while preserving active program uninstallers.
manualSteps: Open Command Prompt as Administrator.
Check C:\Windows\Installer\$PatchCache$\Managed size.
Use SWEEPR Cleaner's Orphaned Installer Scanner to safely purge only unreferenced patch caches.

name: Windows Hibernation File (C:\hiberfil.sys)
warning: Do not delete hiberfil.sys manually. Use 'powercfg /h off' or '/h /type reduced' if you do not use Hibernate on a desktop PC.
whatIsIt: Windows reserves 40% of your total RAM size on your C: drive for C:\hiberfil.sys to support Hibernate and Fast Startup.
whatHappens: On desktop PCs with NVMe SSDs that never use Hibernate, shrinking or disabling hiberfil.sys reclaims 12–32 GB instantly.
manualSteps: Right-click Start and open Terminal (Admin).
To shrink hiberfil.sys by 50% while keeping Fast Startup, run: powercfg /h /type reduced.
To remove hiberfil.sys completely, run: powercfg /h off.

name: Windows Virtual Memory Pagefile (C:\pagefile.sys)
warning: Never force-delete pagefile.sys. It is actively used by the Windows kernel as virtual memory overflow.
whatIsIt: Windows uses C:\pagefile.sys as a virtual memory swap file on your SSD when physical RAM fills up or when writing crash dumps.
whatHappens: Instead of deleting pagefile.sys, clean surrounding cache folders with SWEEPR Cleaner or cap its maximum size in Advanced System Settings if it has ballooned unnecessarily.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type sysdm.cpl and press Enter.
Go to Advanced > Performance Settings > Advanced > Virtual Memory > Change.
Keep a system-managed pagefile on your fastest SSD, or move it to a secondary NVMe drive if C: is critically full.

name: Windows Modern UWP Swapfile (C:\swapfile.sys)
warning: Managed automatically by the Windows memory manager alongside pagefile.sys.
whatIsIt: A small 256 MB dedicated swap file used by Windows 10/11 to suspend and resume Microsoft Store (UWP) apps in the background.
whatHappens: Managed automatically by Windows; focus on cleaning UWP app LocalCache folders instead.
manualSteps: Leave C:\swapfile.sys managed by Windows.
To reclaim space from UWP apps, scan %LocalAppData%\Packages with SWEEPR Cleaner.

name: System Volume Information (VSS Shadow Copies & Restore Points)
warning: Do not modify permissions or delete files inside System Volume Information manually. Use Windows System Protection or vssadmin to prune old restore points.
whatIsIt: Stores Windows System Restore points and Volume Shadow Copy snapshots on your C: drive.
whatHappens: Deleting older superseded restore points while keeping your most recent restore point safely reclaims 10–40 GB.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type sysdm.cpl and press Enter.
Open the 'System Protection' tab, select Local Disk (C:), and click 'Configure'.
Adjust the Max Usage slider (e.g., to 5%) or click 'Delete' to clear outdated restore points.

name: $Windows.~BT & $Windows.~WS Hidden Upgrade Staging Folders
whatIsIt: Hidden root folders created by the Windows 11 Installation Assistant and Media Creation Tool during feature upgrades.
whatHappens: Once your Windows upgrade has finished, deleting $Windows.~BT and $Windows.~WS is 100% safe and reclaims up to 18 GB.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Windows upgrade log files' and 'Temporary Windows installation files'.
Click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows Error Reporting (WER) ReportArchive & ReportQueue
whatIsIt: Whenever an application or service crashes on Windows, WER writes diagnostic archives and heap snapshots into ReportArchive and ReportQueue.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Frees up gigabytes of old crash diagnostic logs.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER and press Enter.
Delete the contents of 'ReportArchive', 'ReportQueue', and 'Temp'.

name: User Application CrashDumps (%LocalAppData%\CrashDumps)
whatIsIt: Windows WER writes full process memory dumps (.dmp) into %LocalAppData%\CrashDumps whenever a game or desktop app crashes.
whatHappens: Completely safe to delete unless you are actively debugging a recent crash in WinDbg.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\CrashDumps and press Enter.
Select all .dmp files (Ctrl+A) and press Delete.

name: Kernel Memory Dump & Minidump (C:\Windows\MEMORY.DMP & Minidump)
whatIsIt: If your PC ever experienced a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD), Windows writes a massive kernel memory dump to C:\Windows\MEMORY.DMP.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete once your system is stable, reclaiming up to 16 GB from a single file.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'System error memory dump files' and 'System error minidump files'.
Click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows File Explorer Thumbnail & Icon Cache (thumbcache_*.db)
whatIsIt: File Explorer caches image, video, and document thumbnails in thumbcache_*.db and iconcache_*.db files that grow continuously over time.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Fixes blank/broken desktop icons and frees up disk space; Windows regenerates thumbnails for active folders on demand.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Thumbnails' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Microsoft DirectX D3DSCache Shader Cache
whatIsIt: Windows' built-in Direct3D shader cache used by DirectX 12 games, browsers, and desktop UI effects.
whatHappens: 100% safe to clean. Removes stale shaders and resolves graphical glitches after Windows updates.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'DirectX Shader Cache' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Component-Based Servicing Logs (C:\Windows\Logs\CBS)
whatIsIt: The Windows Module Installer (TiWorker.exe) writes massive text and .cab archives to C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log and CbsPersist_*.cab.
whatHappens: Deleting old CbsPersist_*.log and .cab files is completely safe and reclaims gigabytes on older Windows installations.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\Windows\Logs\CBS and press Enter (as Admin).
Delete old CbsPersist_*.cab and .log files (skip the currently open CBS.log).

name: DISM & SetupAPI Diagnostic Logs (C:\Windows\Logs\DISM)
whatIsIt: Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM) and driver installations append diagnostic logs in C:\Windows\Logs.
whatHappens: Safe to clean old archive logs to free C: drive space.
manualSteps: Navigate to C:\Windows\Logs\DISM.
Delete archived dism.log.bak files.

name: Windows Setup Panther Upgrade Logs (C:\Windows\Panther)
whatIsIt: Contains diagnostic ETL traces and setupact.log files generated during Windows installation and feature upgrades.
whatHappens: Cleaning old setup log files via Storage Sense / SWEEPR Cleaner safely reclaims disk space.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Windows upgrade log files' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows LiveKernelReports Watchdog Dumps
whatIsIt: When a display driver (TDR) or hardware component briefly hangs and recovers without a blue screen, Windows writes a large .dmp file into C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Reclaims gigabytes of hidden GPU/kernel watchdog dumps.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports and press Enter (as Admin).
Delete all .dmp files inside the WATCHDOG and PoW32kWatchdog subfolders.

name: Microsoft Defender Antivirus Scan History & Support Logs
whatIsIt: Microsoft Defender accumulates years of historical scan results and multi-hundred-MB MPLog-*.log files in ProgramData.
whatHappens: Clearing old scan history logs frees disk space without weakening real-time antivirus protection.
manualSteps: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history to review old items.
Use Disk Cleanup or SWEEPR Cleaner to purge expired Microsoft Defender diagnostic logs.

name: Burn Bootstrapper Package Cache (C:\ProgramData\Package Cache)
warning: Only remove orphaned folders belonging to already-uninstalled Visual C++ Redistributables or SDKs; active WiX Burn installers use Package Cache during uninstallation.
whatIsIt: WiX Burn installers (Visual Studio, .NET SDKs, Python, VC++ Redistributables) cache their original setup executables inside C:\ProgramData\Package Cache.
whatHappens: Removing orphaned caches from uninstalled SDK versions safely frees gigabytes.
manualSteps: First uninstall old SDK or Visual Studio versions via Settings > Apps > Installed apps.
Use SWEEPR Cleaner to identify orphaned Package Cache GUIDs that no longer map to an installed product.

name: Microsoft Office Legacy Local Installation Source (C:\MSOCache)
whatIsIt: Older Microsoft Office MSI installations create a hidden C:\MSOCache folder containing cached cabinet (.cab) setup files.
whatHappens: Can be safely cleaned via Disk Cleanup ('Office Setup Files') once you are on modern Microsoft 365 Click-to-Run.
manualSteps: Run Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe) as Administrator.
Check 'Office Setup Files' if present and click OK.

name: Windows INetCache (Legacy Temporary Internet Files & WebView Cache)
whatIsIt: Desktop applications using the Windows WinINet API cache downloaded installers, RSS feeds, and web assets in %LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Frees disk space used by background desktop updaters.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Temporary Internet Files' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows Font Cache (FontCache-S-*.dat)
whatIsIt: Windows caches rendered glyph outlines for all installed system and Adobe/Figma fonts inside the LocalService FontCache directory.
whatHappens: Safe to rebuild when bloated or corrupted; fixes garbled font rendering in Windows apps.
manualSteps: Stop the 'Windows Font Cache Service' (FontCache) in services.msc.
Delete the FontCache*.dat files inside C:\Windows\ServiceProfiles\LocalService\AppData\Local\FontCache, then restart the service.

name: Windows Certificate CRL & OCSP URL Cache (CryptnetUrlCache)
whatIsIt: Windows caches downloaded SSL certificate revocation lists (CRLs) and Authenticode OCSP responses in CryptnetUrlCache.
whatHappens: Safe to clear; Windows automatically fetches fresh certificate revocation data when verifying signed apps.
manualSteps: Open Command Prompt and run: certutil -urlcache * delete.
This safely flushes stale CryptnetUrlCache entries.

name: Windows System Resource Usage Monitor (C:\Windows\System32\sru)
whatIsIt: Windows logs 30–60 days of per-process network, CPU, and energy usage telemetry into SRUDB.dat inside System32\sru.
whatHappens: Resetting a bloated SRUDB.dat file reclaims space and only clears historical 30-day App History graphs in Task Manager.
manualSteps: Open Task Manager > App history and click 'Delete usage history'.
Or stop the Diagnostic Policy Service (DPS) as Admin to rotate bloated sru logs.

name: Windows DriverStore Superseded GPU & Audio Driver Packages
warning: Never delete folders inside FileRepository manually in File Explorer. Always use pnputil /delete-driver or Windows Storage Sense ('Device driver packages').
whatIsIt: Every time NVIDIA, AMD, or Windows Update installs a new graphics or audio driver, the old 800MB driver package remains in DriverStore\FileRepository.
whatHappens: Cleaning superseded driver packages via pnputil or Storage Sense safely reclaims 5–25 GB without affecting your current active driver.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Device driver packages' and click 'Remove files'.
Advanced users can list unused drivers with: pnputil /enum-drivers.

name: Hidden $Recycle.Bin Corrupted & Per-Drive Trash
whatIsIt: Each NTFS drive maintains a hidden $Recycle.Bin folder partitioned by user SID, which can retain gigabytes of deleted files across multiple accounts.
whatHappens: 100% safe to empty once you have verified you no longer need any deleted files in the Recycle Bin.
manualSteps: Right-click the Recycle Bin on your Desktop and select 'Empty Recycle Bin'.
If corrupted, run in Admin Command Prompt: rd /s /q C:\$Recycle.Bin (Windows recreates a clean folder automatically).

name: Windows Store UWP Apps TempState & AC\Temp (%LocalAppData%\Packages)
whatIsIt: Every Microsoft Store app (Photos, Clipchamp, Xbox, WhatsApp, Paint) has its own sandboxed TempState and AC\Temp directory inside %LocalAppData%\Packages.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete TempState and AC\Temp contents across all UWP packages without resetting app logins.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Packages and press Enter.
Clean the 'TempState' and 'AC\Temp' subfolders inside heavy UWP apps, or run SWEEPR Cleaner to scan all UWP sandboxes at once.

name: Microsoft Clipchamp Video Editor EBWebView & Media Cache
whatIsIt: Windows 11's built-in Clipchamp video editor caches multi-gigabyte video buffers and WebView2 blobs inside its UWP LocalCache.
whatHappens: Safe to clear once your exported MP4 video is saved to your Videos folder.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Clipchamp > Advanced options.
Click 'Reset' after exporting your completed videos, or clean its LocalCache\EBWebView folder.

name: Windows RetailDemo Offline Content Bloat
whatIsIt: Pre-installed store display demo assets shipped on retail Windows 10 and Windows 11 installations.
whatHappens: 100% safe to remove on any personal or work PC.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'RetailDemo Offline Content' if listed and click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows Downloaded Program Files & Legacy ActiveX Cache
whatIsIt: Legacy staging folder used by old web controls and enterprise installers.
whatHappens: Safe to clean via Disk Cleanup or SWEEPR Cleaner.
manualSteps: Run Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe).
Check 'Downloaded Program Files' and click OK.

name: Windows BranchCache Peer Caching Directory
whatIsIt: Enterprise and Windows Pro network cache used to store shared intranet and update payloads.
whatHappens: Safe to flush via netsh branchcache flush or Disk Cleanup.
manualSteps: Open Terminal (Admin) and run: netsh branchcache flush.
This immediately clears all cached BranchCache files.

name: Microsoft Defender Expired Quarantine Items
whatIsIt: Holds neutralized threats and PUA installers quarantined by Microsoft Defender.
whatHappens: Purging old quarantined threats permanently deletes neutralized files and frees disk space.
manualSteps: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history.
Select Quarantined items and click 'Remove' to permanently delete them.

name: Bloated Windows Search Index Database (Windows.edb)
warning: Rebuild the index via Indexing Options rather than deleting Windows.edb while SearchIndexer.exe is running.
whatIsIt: The Windows Search service indexes file contents and Outlook mail into Windows.edb, which can fragment and bloat to 15–25 GB over time.
whatHappens: Rebuilding the index compacts Windows.edb back down to a fraction of its size without losing any user files.
manualSteps: Open Control Panel > Indexing Options > Advanced.
Under Troubleshooting, click 'Rebuild' to compact and recreate a clean search index.

name: WSL2 Linux Virtual Disk Bloat (ext4.vhdx)
warning: Never delete ext4.vhdx directly or you will erase your Linux distribution! Clean /tmp and apt cache inside WSL, then compact the virtual disk.
whatIsIt: Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2) dynamically expands ext4.vhdx as you download files in Linux, but does not automatically shrink it when you delete them.
whatHappens: Cleaning Linux caches and running 'wsl --manage <distro> --set-sparse true' or diskpart compact vdisk safely reclaims tens of gigabytes on Windows.
manualSteps: Inside WSL, run: sudo apt-get clean && sudo rm -rf /tmp/*.
In Windows PowerShell, run: wsl --shutdown.
Compact the virtual disk or use SWEEPR Cleaner to clear surrounding Windows host caches.

name: Leftover NVIDIA Driver Unpack Directory (C:\NVIDIA)
whatIsIt: When you run standalone NVIDIA GeForce driver installers, they extract uncompressed setup files into C:\NVIDIA\DisplayDriver before installing.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete after the driver installation is complete! Your installed NVIDIA driver lives in C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore, not C:\NVIDIA.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer and navigate to Local Disk (C:).
If a folder named C:\NVIDIA exists, right-click it and select Delete.

name: Leftover AMD Radeon Driver Unpack Directory (C:\AMD)
whatIsIt: AMD Radeon Adrenalin and Chipset installers extract their uncompressed setup packages into C:\AMD for every version you've ever installed.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete after driver installation finishes! Your installed AMD drivers are already copied to C:\Program Files\AMD and System32.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer and navigate to C:\AMD.
Delete all old version subfolders inside C:\AMD to reclaim up to 12 GB instantly.

name: Windows SleepStudy & Energy Diagnostic ETL Traces
whatIsIt: Windows records continuous Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) power and Modern Standby sessions in C:\Windows\System32\SleepStudy.
whatHappens: Old historical .etl traces in SleepStudy\ScreenOnPowerStudyTraceSession can be safely purged.
manualSteps: Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\SleepStudy as Administrator.
Remove old archived .etl trace files.

name: Ollama Local LLM Models & Orphaned Blob Cache
whatIsIt: Ollama stores quantized GGUF large language model weights and orphaned layer blobs from interrupted pulls or old model versions on your C: drive.
whatHappens: Removing unused model blobs frees massive SSD space immediately. Models you still use can be re-pulled anytime with 'ollama pull'.
manualSteps: Open Windows Terminal and run 'ollama list' to inspect installed local models.
Remove unused models with 'ollama rm <model-name>', or quit the Ollama tray app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\.ollama\models\blobs, and delete orphaned blob files.

name: LM Studio GGUF Model Cache & Temp Downloads
whatIsIt: LM Studio downloads multi-gigabyte HuggingFace GGUF model checkpoints and temporary partial downloads into your user cache folder.
whatHappens: Deleting unused model folders reclaims tens of gigabytes of SSD space without affecting your LM Studio presets or chat history.
manualSteps: Close LM Studio completely.
Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\.cache\lm-studio\models, and press Enter.
Delete any publisher/model folders you no longer actively run.

name: HuggingFace Hub Transformers & Diffusers Cache
whatIsIt: Python AI tools, Diffusers, and Transformers cache every downloaded safetensors checkpoint and tokenizer snapshot inside .cache\huggingface\hub.

manualSteps: Close any running Python or AI generation terminals.

whatIsIt: ComfyUI writes uncompressed PNG step previews, intermediate workflow latents, and video frame sequences during image and video generation.

name: PyTorch Torch Hub & CUDA Inductors Cache

name: Unity Global Illumination (GI) & Asset Store Cache

whatIsIt: Call of Duty HQ and Warzone store multi-gigabyte DirectX 12 shader packs that grow after every seasonal update and GPU driver change.

whatIsIt: VRChat downloads every custom 3D world and user avatar you encounter into LocalLow\VRChat, rapidly consuming 20GB+ on your C: drive.

name: Windows 11 24H2 Cumulative Checkpoint Update Cache
whatIsIt: Windows 11 24H2 stores differential checkpoint update payloads and uncompressed cab/msu staging files in SoftwareDistribution\Download.

manualSteps: Open Terminal (Admin) and run: net stop wuauserv
Open C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download and delete all files inside.
Restart the Windows Update service with: net start wuauserv

name: Windows ProgramData Package Cache (Visual C++ & MSI Duplicates)
warning: Deleting active installer caches manually can prevent Visual Studio or WiX MSI apps from repairing or uninstalling cleanly. Use SWEEPR Cleaner to target only orphaned caches.

Use SWEEPR Cleaner's Uninstaller Leftovers scan to safely remove only orphaned package folders.

name: Windows Search Index Database (Windows.edb / Windows.db)
whatIsIt: The Windows Search service maintains an indexed database (Windows.edb or Windows.db) that can balloon to 20GB+ due to file churn and Outlook mail indexing.

manualSteps: Open Terminal (Admin) and run: net stop WSearch
Delete Windows.edb / Windows.db inside C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Search\Data\Applications\Windows.
Run: net start WSearch to rebuild a compact, fast search index.

name: Windows DriverStore Temp & Superseded OEM Packages
whatIsIt: Windows stages extracted GPU, chipset, and audio driver packages in DriverStore\Temp during device installation and Windows Update.

Clear C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\Temp or use SWEEPR Cleaner to safely purge superseded driver staging files.

name: Windows CBS (Component-Based Servicing) Persist Logs

name: Windows Desktop Icon Cache Database (IconCache.db)

name: WSL2 Virtual Hard Disk Bloat (ext4.vhdx)
warning: Do NOT delete ext4.vhdx directly or you will lose your entire Linux distribution. Use diskpart compaction or SWEEPR Cleaner to reclaim unallocated disk blocks safely.
whatIsIt: WSL 2 automatically expands the ext4.vhdx virtual hard drive as you install Linux packages, but never shrinks it when files are deleted inside Linux.
whatHappens: Compacting the VHDX file reclaims tens of gigabytes of unallocated free space back to Windows without losing any Linux data.
manualSteps: Open Terminal and shut down WSL: wsl --shutdown
Launch diskpart as Administrator.
Select your ext4.vhdx file and run 'compact vdisk' to recover all unused storage space.

name: Docker Desktop WSL2 Virtual Disk Bloat
warning: Never delete ext4.vhdx in File Explorer. Prune dangling Docker images and compact the virtual disk via diskpart or SWEEPR Cleaner.
whatIsIt: Docker Desktop on Windows uses a dynamic VHDX file inside WSL2 that grows as images and containers are pulled, but never shrinks automatically.
whatHappens: Pruning unused container images and compacting the disk reclaims massive drive space while keeping active containers intact.
manualSteps: Open Windows Terminal.
Run 'docker system prune -a --volumes' to delete dangling images and build layers.
Shut down WSL with 'wsl --shutdown' and compact ext4.vhdx via diskpart.

name: Microsoft vcpkg C++ Library & Binary Cache

Delete the 'archives' and 'downloads' folders to free disk space.

name: Wargaming Game Center Patch & Update Cache
whatIsIt: Wargaming Game Center keeps downloaded client updates and torrent distribution files for World of Tanks and World of Warships.
whatHappens: Frees tens of gigabytes of disk space immediately after game updates finish installing.
manualSteps: Exit Wargaming Game Center from the taskbar tray.
Open C:\ProgramData\Wargaming.net\GameCenter\Updates in File Explorer.
Delete all downloaded patch files inside the Updates folder.

name: Meta Quest Oculus PC Software Download Staging
whatIsIt: The Meta Quest PC app downloads VR software and staging packages into Oculus\Downloads before extracting them.
whatHappens: Safely clears leftover installer staging archives from interrupted or completed VR software installs.
manualSteps: Close the Meta Quest PC app and stop Oculus VR Runtime Service.
Open C:\Program Files\Oculus\Downloads in File Explorer.
Delete lingering staging folders and restart the Oculus app.

name: Windows System32 LogFiles (HTTPERR & Firewall Logs)
whatIsIt: Windows HTTP.sys, Windows Defender Firewall, and IIS store uncompressed HTTP error logs and network connection traces in System32\LogFiles.
whatHappens: Safely deletes old HTTPERR and firewall drop logs, reclaiming gigabytes on your primary Windows drive.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer as Administrator.
Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles.
Open the HTTPERR subfolder and delete historical .log files.

name: Windows Modern Standby & SleepStudy Diagnostics
whatIsIt: Windows laptops track battery drain, Modern Standby sleep transitions, and screen state traces into .etl trace logs in SleepStudy.
whatHappens: Clearing historical sleep study traces frees C: drive space without affecting battery life or power management profiles.
manualSteps: Open Windows Terminal as Administrator.
Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\SleepStudy.
Delete old UserNotPresentSession and ScreenOnSession .etl files.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) Diagnostic Logs
whatIsIt: The Windows WMI repository logs provider query events, CIM repository repairs, and diagnostic traces inside wbem\Logs.
whatHappens: Safely purges historical WMI text logs and resolves drive space constraints without breaking system management services.
manualSteps: Open Terminal as Administrator and run: net stop winmgmt
Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\wbem\Logs and delete old .log files.
Restart the service with: net start winmgmt

name: Windows Routing & Network Tracing Session Logs
whatIsIt: Windows network stack, VPN clients, and Routing and Remote Access (RRAS) write persistent diagnostic logs into C:\Windows\tracing.
whatHappens: Safely deletes accumulated network tracing logs without disrupting current internet or VPN connections.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer as Administrator.
Open C:\Windows\tracing.
Select all .log files and delete them.

name: Windows System Resource Usage Monitor Database
whatIsIt: The System Resource Usage Monitor (SRUM) records network bytes sent/received and application CPU energy consumption in SRUDB.dat.
whatHappens: Resetting a corrupted or oversized SRUDB database resolves Task Manager App History tab freezes and frees SSD storage.
manualSteps: Open Terminal as Administrator and run: net stop DPS
Delete or archive C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat.
Restart the service with: net start DPS

name: Windows Update Session Orchestrator Diagnostic Logs
whatIsIt: The Update Session Orchestrator service writes ETL trace files and diagnostic update logs inside ProgramData\USOShared\Logs.
whatHappens: Safely cleans up stale update orchestration logs and frees SSD space without interfering with Windows Update.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer as Administrator.
Navigate to C:\ProgramData\USOShared\Logs.
Delete old .etl trace files.

name: Adobe Photoshop GPUCache & Dawn WebGPU Cache
whatIsIt: Adobe Photoshop stores compiled Direct3D/Vulkan shader pipelines and WebGPU Dawn cache files that accumulate across app updates.
whatHappens: Cleaning Adobe Photoshop's GPUCache & Dawn WebGPU Cache frees hidden C: drive space and resolves black-screen rendering glitches without logging you out.
manualSteps: Completely quit Adobe Photoshop (verify Photoshop.exe is closed in Task Manager).
Press Windows Key + R, type %AppData%\Adobe\Adobe Photoshop 2025 and press Enter.
Locate GPUCache and DawnCache, select all cached files (Ctrl+A), and press Delete (or clean in 1 click with SWEEPR Cleaner).

name: Adobe Photoshop Code Cache & V8 JavaScript Bytecode
whatIsIt: Adobe Photoshop compiles and caches JavaScript and WebAssembly bytecode locally on disk so UI modules load faster.
whatHappens: Cleaning Adobe Photoshop's Code Cache & V8 JavaScript Bytecode reclaims gigabytes of stale bytecode from old versions while preserving all user settings and accounts.
manualSteps: Completely quit Adobe Photoshop (verify Photoshop.exe is closed in Task Manager).
Press Windows Key + R, type %AppData%\Adobe\Adobe Photoshop 2025 and press Enter.
Locate Code Cache\js and Code Cache\wasm, select all cached files (Ctrl+A), and press Delete (or clean in 1 click with SWEEPR Cleaner).

whatHappens: Cleaning Bruno API Client's GPUCache & Dawn WebGPU Cache frees hidden C: drive space and resolves black-screen rendering glitches without logging you out.
manualSteps: Completely quit Bruno API Client (verify bruno.exe is closed in Task Manager).
Press Windows Key + R, type %AppData%\bruno and press Enter.
Locate GPUCache and DawnCache, select all cached files (Ctrl+A), and press Delete (or clean in 1 click with SWEEPR Cleaner).

name: Bruno API Client Code Cache & V8 JavaScript Bytecode
whatIsIt: Bruno API Client compiles and caches JavaScript and WebAssembly bytecode locally on disk so UI modules load faster.
whatHappens: Cleaning Bruno API Client's Code Cache & V8 JavaScript Bytecode reclaims gigabytes of stale bytecode from old versions while preserving all user settings and accounts.
manualSteps: Completely quit Bruno API Client (verify bruno.exe is closed in Task Manager).
Press Windows Key + R, type %AppData%\bruno and press Enter.
Locate Code Cache\js and Code Cache\wasm, select all cached files (Ctrl+A), and press Delete (or clean in 1 click with SWEEPR Cleaner).
